implementation_notes: Superlinear (degree-5) drift f(X) = -X^5 with multiplicative noise g(X) = X. This is a STABILITY benchmark: no closed-form solution exists, so has_analytic_solution is false and moment expressions are null. Plain Euler-Maruyama DIVERGES here (Hutzenthaler-Jentzen-Kloeden divergence theorem) — its moments blow up and floating point returns Inf/NaN. Use a TAMED Euler scheme: replace the drift increment f(X)*dt by f(X)*dt / (1 + dt*|f(X)|), or use an implicit/adaptive integrator. Note that taming addresses the DRIFT blow-up, which is the actual failure mode; the Milstein correction only improves the diffusion (multiplicative-noise) order and does NOT by itself prevent divergence — any scheme must tame the drift. The independent check verifies only that terminal states X(T) remain finite (no Inf/NaN). Return terminal_paths (shape (num_paths,)) and report empirical mean and variance of X(T) at T=1.
